classification.verdictNote: Designed by Caroline Birk Bahrenscheer, who founded Sætter Copenhagen to make it. Sold direct from Denmark.
classification.summary: The original Sætter cup shelf: a wall-hung type case with 28 cubbies and little pegs between them, made from solid walnut and built by hand in Denmark. Sætter's founder designed it after a flea-market printer's tray, and the shape is now widely copied on Etsy, Amazon and Wayfair. Sold only through Sætter's own store.

quality: Solid walnut throughout, hand-built in Denmark, by the person who designed it. The pegs between cubbies are the signature detail: they hold the dividers and give the grid its rhythm.

Your mugs need to fit a 10 cm wide by 12 cm tall cubby, which suits espresso and standard coffee cups but not wide latte bowls. US orders pay duties and taxes on delivery on top of the $760, so budget extra.

retailers.label: Maker's own store
retailers.notes: In stock on Nov 26. Price excludes US duties and taxes, which are collected on delivery.

maker.name: Sætter Copenhagen
paragraphs: A small Danish furniture brand based north of Copenhagen, founded in 2020 by Caroline Birk Bahrenscheer, an interiors stylist. She bought a worn printer's type tray at a flea market, posted it on Instagram, and was flooded with requests for one; the cup shelf grew from that.
The name means "sets". Sætter designs and produces its shelves in Denmark and sells them from its own store, in oak and walnut, in vertical and horizontal versions.

design.note: The original design, credited to its founder and widely copied.

similar.note: No 'for less' pick: the cheaper peg-style shelves copy Sætter's design. Ferm Living's Tilem is its own design but costs about the same.
